reason: an ACTIVITY_DELTA naming a message that was never created is skipped and MUST NOT fail the run, and it invents no message either — the specification's SHOULD-warn is not asserted because no client emits one today
an ACTIVITY_SNAPSHOT with `replace: false` for an existing activity leaves it as it stands — its content and its activityType both
an ACTIVITY_SNAPSHOT creates the activity message and an ACTIVITY_DELTA patches its content in place
a continuation chunk repeating role with a value its opener did not establish is fatal — the producer has said two incompatible things about one message
a continuation chunk renaming the call its opener established is fatal, not a late correction
chunks expand into the triad — the opener carries the id, the continuation omits it, and the run terminal closes the stream
a continuation chunk MAY repeat toolCallName and parentMessageId as long as the values agree with the opener
a fully conformant 1.0 stream completes without a single warning
a content event for an identifier that is not open is a protocol violation, not a message the consumer invents
a client talking to a current peer declares the protocol version it speaks
CUSTOM ends an open chunk stream, so the id-less continuation that follows has no referent and is fatal
a REASONING_ENCRYPTED_VALUE naming an entity the consumer does not know must not fail the run; the spec lets a consumer drop it, so delivery is deliberately not required
Optional legacy 0.0.39 outgoing media flattening is outside the 1.0-only scope.
Always-on inbound thinking and outbound binary compatibility preserve the shared corpus expectation.
Always-on inbound thinking and outbound binary compatibility preserve the shared corpus expectation.
Optional 0.0.57 subagent downgrade is outside the 1.0-only scope.
Always-on inbound thinking and outbound binary compatibility preserve the shared corpus expectation.
Old-peer declaration omission requires excluded maxProtocolVersion compatibility configuration.
an ordinary event after RUN_FINISHED is fatal — only RUN_STARTED and RUN_ERROR may follow a closed run
a first TEXT_MESSAGE_CHUNK without a messageId is a violation — a consumer must not invent an identifier
a stream that opens with anything but RUN_STARTED or RUN_ERROR is a protocol violation
a first TOOL_CALL_CHUNK must carry both toolCallId and toolCallName; an id alone cannot open a call
RUN_ERROR after RUN_FINISHED is admitted — a failure that surfaced after the run reported success — the failure is delivered to the application as an event, and everything applied before it is kept
a known field carrying a wrong-typed value is fatal, never coerced or ignored
MESSAGES_SNAPSHOT reconciles by id: a message it carries replaces the consumer's copy, and one the consumer holds that it omits is dropped
metadata from every event of a text message merges into it key by key, last write winning, and the merge does not recurse
a second RUN_STARTED while a run is still active is fatal — a producer must close the current run before opening the next
RUN_FINISHED while a text message is still open is fatal — everything the run opened must be closed first
metadata is open by key: vendor-prefixed keys the protocol has never heard of survive untouched and draw no warning, and a null under a key is data rather than an absence
where the schema deliberately leaves an object open, an undescribed member is not unrecognised material: a JSON Patch remove carrying a leftover value arrives whole, applies, and draws no warning
a producer declaring a newer minor of the line this client implements is served, not rejected — the consumer proceeds under the processing model and warns
a producer declaring the version this client speaks is the ordinary case and must pass in silence — the negotiation only speaks up on a difference
a declaration that is not a MAJOR.MINOR identifier cannot be compared, and is handled like a newer one: proceed, and warn
RAW and an unrecognised CUSTOM name are protocol-legal traffic, not unrecognised material: the run completes and nothing warns
RAW stands aside from chunk assembly, so an id-less continuation after one still continues the open stream

a REASONING_MESSAGE_CONTENT with no opener is a streaming-discipline violation and is rejected, exactly as the same shape is for a text message: reasoning messages and spans are bracketed like every other streamed entity, and the consumer does not invent the message an orphaned fragment names
REASONING_MESSAGE_START carrying role 'assistant' is fatal: the schema pins the role to 'reasoning', so any other value is a malformed known value rather than an unrecognised member
a span bracketing one reasoning message assembles into a reasoning-role message in history, alongside the answer it preceded
a closed message is closed, not sealed — a second TEXT_MESSAGE_START for the same id continues it and further content appends

a stream may OPEN with RUN_ERROR — the spec admits it, because a run can fail before it begins — so the client raises no first-event violation; the failure is delivered to the application as an event, and consuming the stream is not itself a failure
RUN_ERROR does not end the stream: a RUN_STARTED after it begins a new run in the same stream, and everything the second run produces is applied and delivered

a cancelled outcome on RUN_FINISHED is described 1.0 material, not something to strip or reject: it survives enforcement without a warning, closes the run rather than failing it, and reaches the application intact, so a consumer can tell a run that was stopped from one that completed — everything delivered before the stop stays delivered
an interrupt outcome on RUN_FINISHED is described 1.0 material, not something to strip or reject: it survives enforcement without a warning, and it closes the run rather than failing it
a run must not finish while an announced invocation is still open — either it ended and was not reported, or the run is not over
a STATE_DELTA amends the snapshot that preceded it, applying its RFC 6902 operations in order
a well-formed patch whose path does not resolve warns, applies nothing at all, and does not fail the run
an operation whose `op` RFC 6902 does not define is an unrecognised union member: the element is dropped from the patch with a warning and the rest of the patch applies
a STATE_SNAPSHOT of `0` replaces the state like any other — state is any JSON value, and a falsy one is not an absent one
a STATE_SNAPSHOT of `null` replaces the state too — the companion falsy case, where an `?? {}` fallback would silently restore an object
a second STATE_SNAPSHOT replaces the state wholesale — nothing of the first survives, and state is any JSON value
STEP_FINISHED for a step that was never opened is fatal
a continuation whose subagentRunId disagrees with its opener's is fatal, because appending one producer's content into another's is undetectable afterwards
SUBAGENT_FINISHED for an invocation never announced is fatal: a lifecycle event closes something, and there is nothing here to close
SUBAGENT_STARTED without a name is fatal: the schema requires it, so its absence is a missing required field, not an optional a consumer may fill in
a subagent's terminal closes the chunk stream still open in its own lane, so the run completes cleanly with the delegated message assembled
attribution without any SUBAGENT_STARTED is legal: a producer may tag work without being able to report the lifecycle, and a consumer must accept it
TOOL_CALL_* metadata accumulates on the tool call itself, not on the assistant message that owns it
start/args/args/end assembles one tool call on its parent assistant message, arguments concatenated in arrival order

a TOOL_CALL_RESULT whose content carries a part sourced from a provider-held file mints a tool message holding that source unchanged — type, handle, provider and mimeType — with no warning; the handle is opaque, so a client may neither rewrite it as a URL nor drop the part for carrying a source arm it does not itself resolve

a TOOL_CALL_RESULT whose content is a list of parts mints a tool message carrying those parts unchanged, placed after the assistant message that made the call, with no warning; asserted on the assembled messages, because the two clients deliver a different event granularity to application code
start/content/content/end assembles one message whose content is the deltas concatenated in arrival order
one stream may carry two runs in sequence, and messages accumulate across the run boundary in order
Reject unknown present text roles, matching the canonical TypeScript and Python SDKs and the shared reference expectation.
an event type the client does not recognise is dropped with a warning and the run survives

an ARRAY in the RUN_FINISHED outcome slot is a malformed value on a described field, so it is fatal — never treated as an unrecognised union member and stripped, which would report success for a run that was paused and lose the interrupt with it
an unrecognised RUN_FINISHED outcome member is stripped from its optional position with a warning, leaving the run to end exactly as an outcome-less RUN_FINISHED does
an unrecognised element inside a list is dropped and the list survives: a user message whose content array carries a future part kind between two text parts keeps both text parts
an undescribed property on a known event is stripped with a warning naming its path, and the event itself survives intact
